clue.text: Tired of backing the family drop out

parts.note: beat is informal for exhausted, worn out

indicators.note: backing here means the word for the family is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with supporting their relatives decides to quit society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the family word round so it is read right to left after the word for tired.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fifties bohemian was a classic societal dropout, rejecting conventional life.

clue.text: Row about poster's boring device

indicators.note: about means the quarrel word goes round the poster word

parts.note: a brawl is a row, a noisy quarrel
an ad is a poster, an advertisement

explanation.surface: An argument erupts over a poster's dull gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed hand tool for making holes in wood, so it bores.

clue.text: No tapas, it turns out, for starters

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner learns there are no tapas to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian appetisers served before the main meal are starters.

clue.text: Girl, as usual, left out

indicators.note: out signals the letter for left is dropped from the word for usual

parts.note: normal means usual, ordinary

explanation.surface: A girl is excluded, as so often happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, as in the Bellini opera heroine.

clue.text: One outcome of a secretary's depression

definitions.text: One outcome of a secretary's depression

parts.words: One outcome of a secretary's depression
parts.note: the depression is pressing a typewriter key, not a low mood

explanation.surface: An office worker's gloom has consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing down a typing button produces a single typed stroke.

clue.text: When a house is thus decorated no payment is asked

definitions.text: When a house is thus decorated no payment is asked

parts.words: When a house is thus decorated no payment is asked
parts.note: a theatre house is filled with free tickets to swell the audience, while the surface suggests wallpapering a home

explanation.surface: A homeowner gets free decorating work done.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre slang a 'house' is the audience; filling it with complimentary tickets is the trick named here, though the surface points at wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre jargon for an audience padded out with free passes, punning on wallpapering a home.

clue.text: Money put down for Highland costume accessory

parts.note: p is a penny, a unit of money
laid means put down, placed

explanation.surface: A deposit is paid for a piece of Scottish dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartan cloth worn over the shoulder is part of Scottish Highland dress.

clue.text: It contains drink for buffet at ball

parts.note: to buffet is to strike, punch
a bowl is a ball rolled in bowling

explanation.surface: A dance's refreshment table holds a vessel of party drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A large serving vessel holds a mixed drink at parties.

clue.text: Certain about the short name of the kidneys

indicators.note: about means the word for certain goes around the short name

parts.note: real means certain, genuine
N is a short form, an abbreviation, of name

explanation.surface: Someone is sure about the abbreviated term for the kidneys.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relating to kidneys comes from the Latin for them.

clue.text: The sun is throwing the quarter deck astray

indicators.note: a quarter of a four-letter word is its first letter
throwing suggests the letters are thrown about into disorder

explanation.surface: On a sunny day a sailor stumbles across the quarterdeck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter deck' is not the ship's deck: a quarter of a four-letter word is its opening letter, which 'throwing' then mixes in with the stray letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic name for the morning star or the sun itself.

clue.text: Awake in a prison

parts.note: stir is slang for jail

explanation.surface: Someone lies sleepless in a jail cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up and moving about means one is no longer sleeping.

clue.text: Votes to shilly-shally

definitions.meaning: ayes and noes cast for and against
to waver indecisively between yes and no

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on an affirmative and a negative together: ballots cast either way, or dithering.

clue.text: Stood still after snake surfaced

indicators.note: after places the stopping word behind the snake word

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
halted means stopped, stood still

explanation.surface: Someone froze on seeing a snake come up out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A road surfaced with tarmac is coated in that black paving material.

clue.text: Scruffy hotel's Spartan servant

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy, so the letters of the hotel are messed up

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An austere servant works in a run-down hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Sparta the serf class who worked the land were state-owned bondsmen.

clue.text: Left mountain to go back for rope

indicators.note: to go back tells us the mountain's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Ossa is a mountain in Greece

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from a peak to fetch climbing rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossa, beside Olympus and Pelion in myth, is a crossword regular; 'to go back' reverses it to ASSO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's noosed line used for catching cattle.

clue.text: Pearl's couch?

parts.note: a pearl grows in a shellfish, and the place where they lie on the sea floor is its resting place

explanation.definitionFit: A seabed area where pearl-bearing molluscs are bred, read as a bed for a pearl.

clue.text: Dicky is not touching the paint

parts.note: off means away from, not in contact with
colour can mean paint, as in a tin of colour

explanation.surface: A decorator warns that it is risky to brush against the wet paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' is British slang for unwell or shaky, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly unwell is described in British slang as dicky.

clue.text: Smoked, and illness pronounced better!

indicators.note: pronounced means the word for illness is used for how it sounds

parts.note: flu is an illness, influenza
cured means made better

explanation.surface: Someone smoked and their illness was declared over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' turns FLU into its sound-alike FLUE, a chimney pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco dried by heat from pipes is cured in this smoked or heated way.

clue.text: Haberdasher has nothing to say about suit

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about puts the speaking word round the suiting word

parts.note: to utter is to say
fit means suit, as clothes do

explanation.surface: A tailor is speechless about a customer's suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of clothing, a men's outfitting shop keeper.

clue.text: Clothes in bottom drawer may be tussore with a posh finish

indicators.note: may be signals the silk's letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: A bride's stored clothes might be made of a fine silk with an upper-class touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges the silk name into TROUSSE. A 'bottom drawer' is the British name for a bride's collection for married life.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's outfit and linen gathered before marriage are kept in the bottom drawer.

clue.text: Bother treasury head over foreign currency

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
head is the first letter of treasury

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: Someone pesters the Treasury chief about overseas money.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconvenience or annoyance; both mean difficulty.

clue.text: In a brawl a thick stick is helpful

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a fight, a heavy club comes in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian police baton made of heavy bamboo is a kind of stick.

clue.text: The popular conception of childhood

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
fancy is an idea or conception

explanation.surface: A common idea of what being young is like.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest stage of life is babyhood.

clue.text: Australia. I found, has invigorating air

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A traveller discovers that Australia has bracing, fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside air was popularly thought to be rich in this bracing form of oxygen.

clue.text: Its winner may be seen in a large limo

definitions.text: Its winner may be seen in a large limo

parts.note: OS is outsize, large
a limo is a car

explanation.surface: A film award winner arrives in a stretch limousine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette, whose winners famously arrive at ceremonies in stretch limousines.

clue.text: Cut short a barrister with this?

definitions.text: Cut short a barrister with this?

parts.words: Cut short a barrister with this?
parts.note: dock means cut short and brief can mean a barrister, while the whole describes instructions handed to counsel from the court's prisoner box

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts a lawyer in mid-speech.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts a prisoner could once hand a fee directly to any barrister present, from the enclosure where defendants stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal instruction given from the prisoner's enclosure directly to counsel in court.

clue.text: Assumption corporation lawyer in US anticipates

indicators.note: anticipates means comes before, so the lawyer precedes the belly

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US lawyer
corporation is old slang for a big belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A company's assumption is anticipated by an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' as a paunch is dated British humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A given fact taken as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Tree trunks found in woods, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, used for its sound

parts.note: in lawn bowls the balls are called woods, or bowls

explanation.surface: Tree trunks are found in forests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woods' is the lawn-bowls name for the balls, a British game.
explanation.definitionFit: The main stems of trees.

clue.text: Advocate with some hesitation appears for scandalmonger

parts.note: to back is to support or advocate
a bit means some, a little
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A lawyer who stammers is taken for a gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spreading malicious talk behind people's backs.

clue.text: Language the French can produce

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: The French are able to produce a language.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Nobleman's dignity represented in melodrama after loss of mother

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's honour is portrayed in an overwrought drama once the mother is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after loss of' signals the mother's letters come out before 'represented' rearranges the rest, ELODRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or title held by a count's British equivalent is a dignity.

clue.text: Kill the sheriff of Bottleneck out of love

indicators.note: out of here means the sheriff is placed outside, wrapping around, the love letter

parts.note: Destry is the sheriff of the town Bottleneck in the Western Destry Rides Again
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Western lawman is driven to murder by spurned love.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottleneck is the town in the film Destry Rides Again.
explanation.definitionFit: To end life or ruin utterly is to wreck or annihilate.
